title: Disputed Korean War kill-ratio evidence cited for OODA tempo advantage
claim_a: Boyd-derived secondary commentary has circulated an approximately 10:1 U.S.-favorable kill ratio for F-86 Sabres against MiG-15s in the Korean War as empirical grounding for the tempo/OODA-cycling thesis. This execution has not independently verified whether Boyd himself stated this exact figure in the primary briefings reviewed (FE-SRC-OODA-001, FE-SRC-OODA-002); the claim's origin within Boyd's own corpus versus later popularizers is unresolved.
claim_b: Hankins (2025), an aviation historian, argues the true Korean War kill ratio was almost certainly lower than 10:1 — though still U.S.-favorable — challenging the strength of this specific empirical anchor for the OODA framework.
limitations: Both the popular claim and the critique are reported at the level of secondary/search-result summary; the underlying historical kill-ratio data was not independently reviewed by this execution.
This record does not resolve which ratio is correct; it preserves the contradiction for future evidence-gathering rather than presenting machine or source agreement as validation.
